questions.stem: What is the main purpose of using standard time zones in a country?
choices: To make time uniform across the country
To make time different in different regions
questions.solution: Standard time zones are used to make time uniform across a country, ensuring that people in different regions follow the same time. The other options are incorrect because they contradict the purpose of time zones.

questions.stem: If the time at the Prime Meridian is 10 a.m., what will be the time at a place located 30° west of the Prime Meridian?
questions.solution: The time decreases by 4 minutes for every degree of longitude west of the Prime Meridian. For 30°, the time difference is 30 × 4 = 120 minutes or 2 hours. Subtracting 2 hours from 10 a.m. gives 8:00 a.m. The other options are incorrect because they do not account for the 4-minute rule or subtract the time incorrectly.

hi.stem: अगर प्राइम मेरीडियन पर समय 10 बजे दोपहर है, तो प्राइम मेरीडियन से 30° पश्चिम में स्थित एक स्थान पर समय क्या होगा?
hi.solution: प्राइम मेरीडियन के पश्चिम में प्रत्येक अक्षांश के लिए समय 4 मिनट कम हो जाता है। 30° के लिए समय अंतर 30 × 4 = 120 मिनट या 2 घंटे होगा। 10 बजे दोपहर से 2 घंटे घटाने पर 8:00 बजे पूर्वाह्न प्राप्त होता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि वे 4 मिनट के नियम को ध्यान में नहीं रखते या समय कम करने में गलती करते हैं।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation is accurate, maintains the same meaning, and uses appropriate terminology. The correct answer is in the same position (option 1), and the distractors remain incorrect.

mr.stem: प्राइम मेरिडियन वर वेळ 10 वाजत असेल, तर प्राइम मेरिडियन पासून 30° पश्चिमेला असलेल्या ठिकाणी वेळ काय असेल?
mr.solution: प्राइम मेरिडियन पासून पश्चिमेला प्रत्येक अंशासाठी वेळ 4 मिनिटे कमी होते. 30° साठी वेळेची फरक 30 × 4 = 120 मिनिटे किंवा 2 तास असेल. 10 वाजापासून 2 तास कमी करून 8:00 दुपारी मिळते. इतर विकल्प चुकीचे असतात कारण ते 4-मिनिटांच्या नियमाला लक्षात घेत नाहीत किंवा वेळ कमी करताना चूक करतात.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the difference in distance between two longitudes?
choices: It is maximum at the equator and decreases towards the poles
It is minimum at the equator and increases towards the poles
It remains the same throughout the globe
questions.solution: The distance between two longitudes is maximum at the equator and decreases as you move toward the poles because the lines of longitude converge at the poles. The first option is incorrect because the distance is not constant everywhere. The third option is wrong because the distance is not smallest at the equator. The fourth option is incorrect because the distance varies across the globe.

questions.stem: If the time at the Prime Meridian is 12:00 noon, what will be the time at a place located 15° west of the Prime Meridian?
questions.solution: The time decreases by 4 minutes for every degree of longitude west of the Prime Meridian. For 15°, the time difference is 15 × 4 = 60 minutes or 1 hour. Subtracting 1 hour from 12:00 noon gives 11:00 a.m. The other options are incorrect because they do not account for the 4-minute rule or subtract the time incorrectly.

questions.stem: Why does the International Date Line not follow the 180° longitude exactly in some places?
choices: To maintain the same day in different regions
To align with the Prime Meridian
questions.solution: The International Date Line deviates from the 180° longitude to avoid crossing large landmasses, which helps prevent confusion in daily life and timekeeping. Maintaining the same day in different regions is not the purpose, as the line is meant to separate different calendar days. Simplifying time calculations is not the main reason, as the line's placement is more about geography than math. Aligning with the Prime Meridian is incorrect because the date line is not connected to that specific line of longitude.
